# Typer classpath corpus audit: Scala 3.9.0

The report is generated from the pinned Scala 3.9.0 audit, which runs once by default. Pass `--verify-determinism` to run it twice and compare normalized output byte-for-byte. It records first blockers for local method typing, isolated Match-case probes, PatDef attempts, and structural inventories. A moved first blocker is not semantic success. The source corpus, parser/namer setup, Scala revision, JDK feature release 21, and classpath remain pinned.

Run `tools/typer-classpath-corpus-audit/run` with the environment documented in `docs/typer-v0.1-compatibility.md` to regenerate this report.

## #946–#950 impure function hardening and next sprint

Historical #950 snapshot: the frozen #946 cohort retained all 13 method observations across 3 `FunctionWithMods` trees in 2 files, with the original one-argument `[Impure]` ordinary-arrow shape and 1 direct / 12 inherited attributions. The old first-blocker count was 13 / 2 files; after #949 it was 0 / 0. Per-row accounting in that snapshot showed all 13 stopping at `SymbolResolution`; none was fully typed. The source-type cache was rolled back with each enclosing failed method transaction, so the snapshot’s `projection=not_completed` column meant no projected root type was published after that method attempt. Focused source projection regressions verified that the impure alias was selected and preserved before normalization; the corpus result was bounded by symbol resolution. The figures and recommendation in this section record the #950 snapshot and are not recalculated by this script.

The full structural census still contains `FunctionWithMods` trees independently of first blockers. It also counts plain ordinary `Function` trees, which represent pure ordinary arrows in the parser. Modifier and family distributions, erased-parameter count, and `CapturesAndResult` adjacency appear in `function_with_mods_structural_inventory` below. Structural presence is not counted as a first-blocker failure.

In the #950 snapshot, the audit had 0 / 3,297 typed local methods. The #946 cohort moved 13 / 13 to the resolution/classpath family. External member requests rose from the prior 7,582 baseline to 7,802, while materialized external members remained 0; recent source-function and inferred-field cohorts also terminated repeatedly at `SymbolResolution` or `ImportQualifierNotFound`. The semantic rank was separate: anonymous class instantiation led at 32 / 15 files, followed by local type definitions and `SymbolSourceKindMismatch` at 11 each.

### Recommendation: import and classpath resolution sprint

The #950 snapshot recommended the import/classpath resolution sprint. It is broader than implementing anonymous classes, the highest single Typer-owned bucket, but it addressed the measured ceiling affecting the entire #946 cohort and multiple earlier cohorts: 7,802 external member requests produced zero materialized members, and 13 / 13 impure-function rows reached `SymbolResolution`. Anonymous classes were a bounded alternative at 32 / 15 files but required identity, owner, `ClassInfo`, and constructor/parent lowering. The compact semantic candidates ranked at 11 or fewer and would still have left the shared resolution gate untouched. This was a recommendation for the next sprint only; resolution implementation was outside #950.

## #802–#806 local extension hardening

The initial local-extension blocker was 25 occurrences in 5 files. The current audit splits extension-specific failures from ordinary local method signatures. It attempted 3,297 local method definitions and fully typed zero; moved failures are not counted as semantic success. Focused tests cover a fully typed local extension call, nominal-member precedence, local shadowing, unsupported receiver/signature forms, rollback, and bounded ambiguity.

| Focused extension failure bucket | Count / files | Representative paths |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `LocalExtensionGroupShapeDeferred` | 3 / 1 | compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/Applications.scala |
| `LocalExtensionReceiverTypeNotFound` | 1 / 1 | compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/core/Flags.scala |
| `LocalExtensionSignatureDeferred::dependent result types` | 1 / 1 | compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/reporting/MessageRendering.scala |

Receiver or ordinary-argument mismatches remain non-applicable candidates and preserve `MemberNotFound`; the audit does not relabel those as successful typing. Multiple viable same-name local extensions produce `OverloadedSelectionDeferred` in a focused regression. Primitive definitions have no modeled member scopes. If nominal lookup cannot inspect a primitive member index, local extension resolution is not attempted and the original `MemberLookup` error is retained; fallback is available only after a completed index confirms that the ordinary name has no member. External member materialization remains zero.

### #929 local value baseline and #930–#932 implementation status

The pinned #929 baseline attributes 21 first-blocker observations across 8 files to 14 distinct `ValDef` declarations; none are `PatDef`. Five declarations produce repeated sibling-method observations, accounting for 7 observations beyond the first observation for each declaration; all 21 rows are inherited observations from the enclosing method attempt. The exact method/declaration pairs, source spans, full source modifiers, type form, RHS, visibility, annotations, and attribution remain in the historical #929 cohort below. Following #930, ordinary local values preserve `FINAL`/`MUTABLE` flags and contextual modifiers are validated. #931 types direct named `implicit val` and named `given` declarations, preserves their mapped flags, and inserts them into lexical scope after a successful initializer. #932 types direct local lazy vals through the same path and preserves `LAZY`; no runtime initialization or lowering structures are synthesized. Contextual search/insertion, recursive lazy type inference, explicit recursive lazy warning analysis, and forward references to later lazy declarations remain unsupported. Anonymous givens have no local term identity and report `LocalValueModifierDeferred::anonymous given has no local term identity`. The complete 21-row cohort is retained individually in `local_value_baseline_outcomes`: 4 rows stop at the anonymous-given boundary, 16 currently have `ImportQualifierNotFound` as their enclosing-method first blocker with no completed local-symbol mapping, and one inline row retains a focused modifier deferral. The current generic local-value blocker is that one `inline val` observation.

### #933 hardening result and next-sprint recommendation

The full #929 cohort is checked row-by-row: 21 observations, 14 source declarations, and 8 files. None of these source declarations is a `PatDef`, so no baseline row moved into a PatDef-specific blocker. The generic local `val`/`var` bucket is now 1 / 1 (the remaining inline value); the selected contextual and lazy declaration families retain focused flag, identity, scope, shadowing, rollback, and repeated-typing coverage. The audit still reports 0 / 3,297 fully typed local methods. Current resolution/classpath blockers are `ImportQualifierNotFound` 2,892 / 274 files, `TypeNameNotFound` 80 / 30, `MemberLookup` 61 / 28, and `SymbolResolution` 40 / 17. Sixteen of the 21 cohort rows stop at `ImportQualifierNotFound`; the other five remain at four anonymous-given deferrals and one inline-value deferral. The classpath gate remains separate: 7,582 external member requests produced 0 external member symbols.

| Candidate | Measured reach | Risk and reuse | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anonymous classes | 32 observations / 15 files | High identity, ownership, and class-info risk; ordinary `new` typing is reusable | Highest reach, but broadest architectural slice |
| Remaining local values / PatDef | 1 generic `inline val` observation / 1 file; no PatDef in the pinned #929 cohort | Inline constant evaluation is absent; general destructuring is a larger separate feature | The bounded ordinary/contextual/lazy families are complete, so the residual reach is small or semantically broad |
| `FunctionWithMods` | 13 observations / 2 files | Compact type-tree family with existing function-type projection as a starting point; needs pinned syntax and conformance tests | Bounded reach with lower ownership risk |
| Import/classpath resolution | 7,582 external member requests / 0 materialized members | Crosses class loading, binary projection, and member resolution; repeatedly blocks otherwise-unlocked methods | Dominant reachability gate, but requires a broader resolver sprint |

**Recommended next sprint: `UnsupportedTypeTree::FunctionWithMods`.** It covers 13 observations in two files with a bounded type-tree shape and reuses the existing function-type path. Anonymous classes have greater raw reach but substantially higher identity/ownership risk; remaining local values offer only one inline observation without compile-time semantics; classpath resolution blocks the most methods but spans a much wider subsystem.

## Historical #825 MissingDeclaredType producer profile (pre-#856)

Before #856, the 34 first blockers across 15 files were all attributed to source `ValDef` declarations with a right-hand side and a zero-width synthetic inferred `TypeTree`. They split into 24 immutable values and 10 mutable variables; all have semantic `Field` identity. Source `val` versus `var` comes from the AST modifier and is cross-checked against the semantic `MUTABLE` flag; `SymbolKind::Field` alone does not preserve that distinction. The owner kind is `Class` for 24 occurrences and `ModuleClass` for 10. Four immutable module-class values carry `Inline`. The frozen #972 cohort had 342 `UnresolvedSupertype` errors across 33 requested classes and 79 files. After #974, 212 remain across 26 classes and 51 files; total member errors fall from 347 to 217 while requests rise from 7,895 to 8,070 as resolution proceeds deeper. The eight root families that no longer fail are `dotty/tools/io/AbstractFile`, `scala/Function1`, `scala/collection/AbstractIterator`, `scala/collection/IterableOnce`, `scala/collection/Iterator`, `scala/collection/SpecificIterableFactory`, `scala/concurrent/duration/Duration`, and `scala/math/Ordering`. Newly exposed failures include `dotty/tools/io/VirtualDirectory` and additional requests for `scala/annotation/retainsCap`; these are counted as remaining failures, not fixes. The 5 separate unresolved-class errors are also retained in the result.

The `tasty_unresolved_supertype_failures` rows below now include the parent index, structured shape, semantic-reference and explicit-prefix flags, visible name-table spellings, and compact raw-tree tag shape. The real Scala 3.9 `Source.tasty` integration fixture covers an applied parent through the package-object alias path. Unresolved semantic references continue to fail without a same-package guess.

## #976 audit gate and dependency profile

The final pinned Scala 3.9/JDK 21 audit ran twice; normalized reports matched byte-for-byte. The frozen #972 request-shape cohorts, #973 generic-signature cases, #974 TASTy parent cases, #975 class/member gate, and #946/#826–#829/#856–#858/#880/#899/#929 rows remain represented in this report. Local methods remain 0/3,297. `ImportQualifierNotFound` remains the largest first blocker at 2,908 observations across 277 files and is classified under resolution/classpath environment. This is distinct from the Typer-owned semantic ranking, where `AnonymousClassInstantiationDeferred` leads at 32 observations in 15 files.

The resolver-side member outcome breakdown is `class member scope unavailable: incomplete class info` 3,771, `package term member unsupported` 2,749, `unsupported prefix shape` 503, `package type member unresolved` 402, external class success 358, load error 217, other resolver miss 68, and other success 2. These request outcomes identify the dominant unresolved shapes behind the classpath ceiling; they are aggregate measures alongside first-blocker counts, not a one-to-one attribution of each `ImportQualifierNotFound` observation.

The class gate passes its external-class threshold: 358 class-symbol successes across 29 distinct classes. External non-class member successes remain 0; 7,493 member requests are unresolved and 217 fail during loading. Package-term lookup produced 2,749 unsupported outcomes for 80 request keys across 115 files. Although the classpath contains type-side resources for 2,212 requests/51 keys and companion `$` resources for 2,196 requests/46 keys, neither resource alone establishes canonical module identity. The frozen rows and full request-shape breakdown remain in the raw data below.

Opt-in dependency profiling observed 958 top-level class loads: median nested depth 0, p95 140, maximum 141, and a maximum fanout of 1,048 distinct classes in one request. The largest roots are repeated `dotty/tools/io/AbstractFile` requests from classpath and TASTy operations. This long tail is evidence of eager transitive-loading cost. **Next sprint recommendation: investigate lazy/deferred dependency completion**, and use the profile to verify the tail reduction. Package term/object materialization remains a separate identity boundary. The source-typing rollback regression asserts the store checkpoint, typed tree and source-type mappings, package links, declaration scopes, and clean class identity on retry.
